name: Nauo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Schurmann, Clamor W. 1844. A vocabulary of the Parnkalla language.. to which is prefixed a collection of grammatical rules. Adelaide: Dehane. (NLA scanned, held under bang1339)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Gives accent rules for BARNGARLA/Parnkalla only (penult in disyllables, antepenult in words of 3+ syllables, verbs keep root accent); the headword 'nauo' is just the tribe name. Not a Nauo source; noted only as the neighbouring-language description by the same recorder.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request 2011-133 (split [wiw]; create [nwo] Nauo, [wgu] Wirangu). SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; states there is no significant body of literature or research for Nauo and relies on Hercus & Simpson 2001.

sources.citation: Hercus, Luise & Jane Simpson. 2001. The tragedy of Nauo. In J. Simpson, D. Nash, M. Laughren, P. Austin & B. Alpher (eds), Forty years on: Ken Hale and Australian languages, 263-290. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics (PL 512). DOI 10.15144/PL-512.263.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The article reproduces the entire Nauo corpus (Schurmann's 7 lexemes + 3 inflected forms, Tindale's 3 words from Frank Kent 1927, placenames) and its only phonological content is phonotactic (Table 5, p.283: vowel-final words, initial ty, i-u sequences, absence of prestopping). The single occurrence of the word 'stress' (fn.16, p.272) concerns Provis's acute accent on a Venus Bay Kukatha/Wirangu form, not Nauo.

sources.citation: Hercus, Luise. 1999. A grammar of the Wirangu language from the west coast of South Australia. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics C-150. Sec. 1.4(d) 'Nauo (Nyawa)', pp.13-14.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL7101.W55 H4 1998)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL7101.W55 H4 1998
sources.note: Nothing on Nauo phonology; states 'all we have is eight words from Schurmann (1846:28-29) and a few verb forms, as well as a few words from Tindale (1928 and 1939)'.

sources.citation: Schurmann, Clamor W. 1846 [repr. 1879]. The Aboriginal tribes of Port Lincoln in South Australia. In J. D. Woods (ed.), The native tribes of South Australia, 207-251. Adelaide: E. S. Wigg. (archive.org scanned text of nativetribessou00taplgoog; Nauo passage printed pp.249-250)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The primary record of Nauo: a 10-item Parnkalla/Nauo/English table plus 'seems to deviate from the Parnkalla by a broader and harsher pronunciation' and 'Both dialects terminate every word with a vowel'. No accent/stress remark for Nauo.

sources.citation: Mobile Language Team (University of Adelaide). Nawu language page. https://mobilelanguageteam.com.au/languages/nawu/
sources.note: Nothing; reports a reconstructed 'Nhawu' vocabulary (300 words) built from Schurmann's 10 recorded words; no pronunciation or stress information.

sources.citation: Simpson, Jane & Luise Hercus. 2004. Thura-Yura as a subgroup. In C. Bowern & H. Koch (eds), Australian languages: classification and the comparative method, 179-206 (+ appendix 580-645). Amsterdam: John Benjamins.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Only other modern treatment naming Nauo; might state a proto-Thura-Yura or family-wide (initial) stress generalisation, but cannot add first-hand Nauo data beyond the 13 forms. Low expected yield.

sources.citation: Tindale, Norman B. 1928 / 1939. Field journals and vocabulary cards (Nauo words from Frank Kent, Coffin Bay), South Australian Museum Archives AA 338.

sources.note: The only other primary Nauo material (three words); conceivably carries Tindale's stress diacritics on individual forms, though Hercus & Simpson 2001 reproduce the forms without any.
